sentences.text: IBAC’s Operation Harmonia investigated allegations that senior officers at the former Department of Jobs, Precincts and Regions failed to address or report losses from COVID-19 business support grants.
sentences.support: failed to act on internal and external indicators of fraud, corruption and other losses

sentences.text: It examined the treatment of backdated GST registrations and information provided to ministers, the Auditor-General and the Victorian Ombudsman.
sentences.support: Over the course of this investigation IBAC also considered the provision of information to the Victorian Ombudsman

sentences.text: IBAC found that senior officers withheld information about a suspected $285 million loss from the secretary and minister, preventing them from considering a response.
sentences.support: compromised the government’s ability to develop an appropriate response to address the suspected loss of $285 million in public funds

sentences.text: IBAC also found that information was withheld from the Ombudsman and misleading information was given to an incoming minister.
sentences.support: The investigation also found that Executive Director A withheld key information from the Ombudsman

sentences.text: IBAC made no recommendations, emphasising the need for frank advice and a culture that supports staff raising concerns.
sentences.support: IBAC has not made recommendations in this instance but notes that fostering an environment in which providing frank and fearless advice is valued

findings.quote: IBAC’s investigation found that critical information was withheld from the Secretary and the Minister, contrary to the public sector values of integrity and responsiveness.
IBAC found that a letter provided to the Victorian Ombudsman withheld key information about the department’s method for assessing GST registration.

notes: Loss figures are described as suspected, as in the report. No finding of criminal guilt is implied.
